summary: The EU lists Poland among the Schengen area countries. EU law says Member States let Union citizens enter with a valid identity card or passport and may impose no entry visa on them; the EEA Agreement extends this to nationals of the EFTA States. Nationals of the countries listed in Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period, and nationals of the countries listed in Annex I must hold a visa; ETIAS is currently not in operation. The Visa Code sets the visa fee at €90.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any rolling 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area rather than per country. The Schengen Borders Code counts the day you arrive as the first day of stay and the day you leave as the last. Leaving and coming back does not reset the allowance: the Schengen Borders Code counts the 180-day period preceding each day of stay, so days already spent anywhere in the area during that period still count against the 90.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Poland?
faq.answer: No visa is needed for a short stay: the United States is among the countries whose nationals Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 exempts from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period. ETIAS, which will require visa-exempt travellers to have a travel authorisation, is currently not in operation; its website lists a EUR 20 application fee.

faq.question: How much does a Poland Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The Visa Code sets the visa fee at €90, and €45 for children from the age of six and below the age of 12; the fee is waived for children under six. It says applications are decided within 15 calendar days, a period that may be extended up to a maximum of 45 calendar days in individual cases. Poland's Foreign Ministry says the uniform Schengen visa permits a stay in all Schengen countries of a maximum of 90 days during a 180-day period.

faq.question: Can Ukrainian citizens enter Poland without a visa?
faq.answer: Yes, with a biometric passport: Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 exempts Ukrainian nationals from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period, limited to holders of biometric passports issued by Ukraine in line with ICAO standards.

faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says the currency of Poland is the zloty (PLN).

levies.name: Local visitor fee (opłata miejscowa)
levies.exemptions: Not charged (on reciprocity) to staff of diplomatic missions and consular offices and persons treated as equal to them, if they are not Polish citizens and do not live permanently in Poland; to people staying in hospitals; to blind people and their guides; to people paying property tax on summer houses in the locality; and to organised groups of children and school youth.
levies.text: A municipal council may introduce a local fee, charged to natural persons staying more than a day for tourist, holiday or training purposes in qualifying localities, for each started day of stay. The cap on the rate is announced for each tax year. For 2026 the caps are PLN 3.46 a day (localities referred to in art. 17(1)(1)) and PLN 4.89 a day (localities with spa-protection-area status).
